2607.15957.title: From Plausible to Actionable: A Position on LLM Self-Explanations
2607.15957.paper_summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate natural language explanations that rationalize their own decisions, a phenomenon commonly referred to as self-explanations.Such explanations have emerged as a promising direction for explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), particularly for interpreting LLM behavior.However, while self-explanations often appear plausible, whether they faithfully reflect a model's underlying reasoning process remains an open question. In this opinion paper, we argue that self-explanations can be highly plausible, questionably faithful, and yet highly actionable. From a traditional XAI perspective, we identify the limitations of standard evaluation protocols for LLM-generated self-explanations and propose practical guidelines for assessing their plausibility and faithfulness. Moreover, we argue that evaluation should extend beyond these criteria to actionability, highlighting applications of LLM rationalization capabilities that support informed decision-making and appropriate action across diverse stakeholders.
2607.15957.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）可以生成自然語言解釋，來合理化它們自己的決策，這種現象通常被稱為自我解釋。<lb/>這類解釋已成為可解釋人工智慧（XAI）的一個有前景的方向，特別是在解釋LLM行為方面。<lb/>然而，儘管自我解釋常常看起來合理，但它們是否忠實反映模型的基本推理過程仍然是一個未解之問。<lb/>在這篇意見文章中，我們主張自我解釋可以非常合理、可疑地忠實，卻又高度可行。<lb/>從傳統的XAI視角來看，我們確定了標準評估協議對LLM生成的自我解釋的限制，並提出了評估其合理性和忠實性的實用指導方針。<lb/>此外，我們主張評估應超越這些標準，延伸到可行性，強調LLM合理化能力的應用，支持各種利益相關者的知情決策和適當行動。
